## Symptom

A work-item write "succeeds" but nothing persists. Classic tell: `release {claimHold:true}`
returns ok, yet `work_items:get` shows `payload:{}` and the item keeps getting re-served by
`scheduler:get_next` (EI-15345 / WI-1281 re-served ~2h apart, twice, despite repeated holds).
The scheduler read-side is a red herring — it correctly applies the `_claimHold` feature floor
(`claimFloorsWhereSql`). The bug is write-side.

## Root cause — the WI-5261 lost-ALS-scope class

`activeWorkspaceId()` resolves the request's workspace from AsyncLocalStorage. Several `await`s
deep in a tool call chain (e.g. release handler → releaseOne → `setWorkItemClaimHold`), the ALS
request scope can be **lost**, so `activeWorkspaceId()` silently falls through to the
process-global default (`workspace-registry.ts`; "confirmed live for papercusp-workspace,
2026-07-17").

If a write derives its target workspace from that bare `activeWorkspaceId()` (or an item lookup
like `getWorkItem`/`getFeatureWorkItemOnly` that PINS to it), and the resolved value doesn't match
the item's OWN workspace, the `WHERE workspace_id = …` matches zero rows — the write no-ops. With
an INSTEAD OF view trigger in the path, `RETURNING` can even echo a "success" payload while the
inner table UPDATE matched nothing.

`scheduler/get-next.ts` was already hardened against this (WI-5261): it threads the caller's
resolved workspace via `opts.workspaceId` instead of trusting `activeWorkspaceId()`. Sibling write
paths that trust the ambient value are still exposed.

## Fix pattern

Resolve the item's ACTUAL workspace by id, ambient-independent, then scope the write to it:

```
-- sql-snippet-justified: IMPLEMENTATION pattern for the write path itself (resolving an
-- item's own workspace before writing) — it is what a tool must do, not a read to run.
SELECT harness_slug, workspace_id
  FROM harness_shared.work_items
 WHERE feature_id = ${id} AND ${harness ? sql`harness_slug = ${harness}` : sql`TRUE`}
 ORDER BY (workspace_id = ${activeWorkspaceId()}) DESC, updated_ts DESC NULLS LAST
 LIMIT 1
```

The `(workspace_id = active) DESC` primary sort still PREFERS the active-workspace row when present
(unchanged healthy behavior + disambiguates a cross-workspace id collision, F-B3), but falls back
to the item's real row when the ambient value is wrong. Then `UPDATE … WHERE workspace_id = <that
row's workspace_id> AND feature_id = ${id}`. Never `WHERE workspace_id IN (issuesScopeWorkspace(),
activeWorkspaceId())`.

## When you hit this

Any work-item mutation that keys on `workspace_id` and runs deep in a tool handler. Grep for
`activeWorkspaceId()` / `issuesScopeWorkspace()` used directly in a write's WHERE. If the write can
run for an item whose workspace differs from the caller's window, it's exposed — resolve by id.

## Test-schema caveat

`work-items-claim-hold.integration.test.ts` uses an INVERTED schema: `work_items` is the BASE table
(PK `(harness_slug, feature_id)`, no workspace column) and `harness_features_consolidated` is a
passthrough view — the opposite of production (`work_items` is a UNION view over the two family
tables with an INSTEAD OF trigger). So that harness cannot represent the same id in two workspaces;
exercise the workspace-mismatch case with the ambient `activeWorkspaceId()` mock set to a workspace
that differs from the seeded item's.
